name: India
oneLiner: Meyer classes India as hierarchical and top-down but open to revising decisions, and culture splits by type of business.
intro: India has rich statistics on developer numbers and employment, from NASSCOM, USCIS and GitHub Octoverse, plus news reports. Sources on review and retrospective practice are mostly anecdotes and industry articles. The tendencies are national, and culture differs widely between the large IT services firms, foreign-owned global capability centers (GCCs) and product startups.

design.text: TCS announced in 2011 that it had been assessed at CMMI Level 5 enterprise-wide for both CMMI-DEV and CMMI-SVC. It says it was the first company in the world to reach enterprise-wide Level 5 for SVC.

sources.title: TCS: First software firm assessed at Level 5 enterprise-wide in software services and development

design.text: Hiring-industry articles contrast services firms ("specs are king, process-heavy, ticket-driven") with product companies ("design docs, code review, CI/CD"). Neither is backed by research.

sources.title: Uplers: Product vs Service-Background Engineers
ProductBased.in: Product Based vs Service Based Companies in India

design.text: The idea that jugaad (improvised fixes under constraints) is a virtue in software development draws criticism from Indian engineers themselves, on Hacker News and elsewhere. Others defend it as frugal engineering, such as designing apps that work on 2G connections.

sources.title: Hacker News: Jugaad takes agile to the extreme
Sujay Pan: The Cult of Jugaad
Why India's Jugaad Coding Culture Might Save Bloated Software

design.text: Zerodha is India's largest stockbroker, yet its tech team of 33–35 people self-hosts the entire stack. CTO Kailash Nadh says it is a misconception that team size must grow in proportion to the number of users.

sources.title: Software Misadventures: Kailash Nadh
Indian Startup News: Zerodha hired only 5 employees for its tech team in 4 years

failure.text: Meyer's 2017 HBR article says that in top-down decision-making cultures, India among them, decisions are made quickly but can change as new input or arguments arise. A decision is treated as a placeholder that can be adjusted later, not a firm commitment.

sources.title: Erin Meyer, Being the Boss in Brussels, Boston, and Beijing (HBR)

failure.text: On Meyer's Scheduling scale, India is on the flexible-time side. People there are described as running several things in parallel, accepting interruptions and putting adaptation first.

sources.title: Welcome to the Jungle: The 8 keys for managing multicultural teams by Erin Meyer

failure.text: The claim that offshore teams do not escalate bad news rests on anecdotes on Hacker News. Other HN commenters counter that US-side managers often have not built a structure that invites pushback.

sources.title: Ask HN: What challenges are you facing offshoring development to India?
Hacker News discussion on pushback

feedback.text: An article summarizing Meyer's eight scales places India toward the high-context end and on the side that avoids confrontation.

sources.title: Welcome to the Jungle: The 8 keys for managing multicultural teams by Erin Meyer

feedback.text: Rastogi et al. (ESEM 2018) analyzed about 70,000 GitHub pull requests. In 16 of 17 countries, pull requests were more likely to be accepted when submitter and reviewer shared a country. India was the exception, with acceptance 7.4% lower when the maintainer was also Indian.

sources.title: Relationship between Geographical Location and Evaluation of Developer Contributions in GitHub (summary, WWS2019)

hierarchy.text: Meyer's 2017 HBR article places India in the top-down, hierarchical quadrant, together with Brazil, China, France, Indonesia, Mexico, Russia and Saudi Arabia.

sources.title: Erin Meyer, Being the Boss in Brussels, Boston, and Beijing (HBR)

hierarchy.text: India scores 77 on Hofstede's power distance (PDI), its highest of the six dimensions. The Culture Factor describes this as an appreciation of hierarchy and top-down structure.

sources.title: The Culture Factor — Country comparison tool

hierarchy.text: A hiring-industry article contrasts services firms, which run on approval chains and hierarchy, with product startups, where engineers can talk to founders directly and decisions are fast.

sources.title: Uplers: Product vs Service-Background Engineers

communication.text: In the EF EPI 2024, India ranked 69th of 116 countries and regions. English is widely used as a working language, but India sits mid-table on this test.

sources.title: Nippon.com: Japan Slides Further in English Proficiency Ranking

communication.text: Explainers of Meyer's Trusting scale place India on the relationship-based side, where trust built through personal relationships is needed before work begins.

sources.title: The Erin Meyer Culture Map Explained

work.text: NASSCOM estimated India's tech industry revenue for FY2025 at about $282.6 billion, with 5.8 million employees (a net addition of 126,000). A 2026 revision raised the figures to $297 billion and 5.82 million.

sources.title: Business Today: Indian tech industry to reach $300 billion revenue milestone in FY26
DQIndia: Nasscom outlook FY26

work.text: NASSCOM and Zinnov count more than 1,700 global capability centers (GCCs) of foreign companies in India as of FY2024, employing more than 1.9 million people. GCCs are also spreading to tier-2 cities.

sources.title: NASSCOM: India GCC Landscape Report — The 5-year Journey
NASSCOM: Beyond the Metros

work.text: Attrition at the large IT services firms swings with the business cycle. In Q2 FY23 it was 27.1% at Infosys, 23% at Wipro and 21.5% at TCS. By Q4 FY24 it had fallen to 12.5% at TCS and 12.6% at Infosys.

sources.title: Business Today: TCS, Infosys, Wipro — How HR issues plague IT sector
Business Standard: TCS, Infosys, Wipro see exit of 64,000 employees in FY24

work.text: USCIS data show that 72.3% of H-1B petitions approved in FY2023 were for people born in India, against 11.7% for people born in China.

sources.title: USCIS: Characteristics of H-1B Specialty Occupation Workers FY2023
Pew Research: What we know about the U.S. H-1B visa program

work.text: In 2023, Infosys founder Narayana Murthy said young Indians should work 70 hours a week. The remark drew strong backlash on social media but support from some business leaders, and opinion split.

sources.title: CNBC: India debate on 70-hour workweek
Business Today: Narayana Murthy's remark leaves internet divided

oss.text: GitHub Octoverse 2025 counts 21.9 million developers in India, second only to the US and up from 4.5 million in 2020. More than 5 million joined in 2025 alone.

sources.title: GitHub Octoverse 2025

oss.text: The same Octoverse 2025 report says India has already overtaken the US to have the world's largest base of public and open source contributors, and projects 57.5 million developers in India by 2030.

sources.title: GitHub Octoverse 2025

oss.text: Zerodha launched FLOSS/fund in October 2024 to give $1 million a year to open source projects worldwide. In 2025 it paid out a total of $1 million to projects including Blender, FFmpeg and OpenSSL.

sources.title: Entrepreneur: Zerodha launches USD 1 Mn annual fund
Open Source For You: Zerodha announces final $675,000 tranche

oss.text: Zerodha CTO Kailash Nadh says India uses FOSS heavily but its contributions are negligible, and has proposed a government-backed sovereign FOSS fund.

sources.title: Analytics India Magazine: India's FOSS contributions remain negligible

variance: Process, hierarchy and pace differ widely between the large IT services firms (TCS, Infosys, Wipro), foreign GCCs and product startups. Moving from a services firm to a GCC is described as a common career path.
Companies such as Zerodha run huge systems with small teams, which runs against the image of India as a country that throws headcount at problems.
The common claim that an Indian "yes" does not mean agreement has no support beyond anecdotes, so this page leaves it out.
India has one of the largest developer populations, but voices within India say the depth of its open source contribution does not match its numbers.
No systematic data was found on postmortem culture.
In the Stack Overflow Developer Survey 2024, 7.2% of respondents were from India, the third-largest share, so India is far better represented in international surveys than Japan or South Korea.
Octoverse 2025's 2030 projection is inconsistent. Its chart shows 54.7 million developers for the US and 57.5 million for India, but its text puts the US at "more than 40 million."
